$comment: The contract of .agents/harness.config.json, the one file that holds this project's harness settings and facts. pnpm verify:harness-config holds the file to it, reading only the keywords it knows (type, properties, items, required, additionalProperties, enum, const, minLength, if, then, else, and the annotations $schema, $comment, title, description and default) and refusing any other, so a rule written here is never skipped in silence. additionalProperties is true or false, never a schema, and every object outside an if, then or else sets it to false, so every key the file holds is one declared here; neither file gives a key twice in one object. A default is the value the template ships and the one a skill assumes when the file records none; each must be one of its own enum. See docs/harness.md section 3h.
title: Harness config
description: The project's harness settings and facts: its identity, workflow, merge policy and backend, and, when it records them, its vocabulary, stack, portable core and skill trees.

$schema.description: The path of this contract, relative to .agents/, so an editor checks the file as it is typed.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the file.

identity.description: The names of the project, the one block a derived repository rewrites to name itself: a gate that keeps a product's names out of a portable part of the harness reads its terms here.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

product.description: The product's name, as people write it.

repository.description: The repository's name on its host, with or without its owner.

packageScope.description: The npm scope of the workspace packages, with its @ and no slash, such as @app.

workflow.description: How a change is specified and recorded (decision 40).

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

mode.description: sdd: OpenSpec in the repository, chosen by size (openspec/README.md). odd: the feature-document workflow, its document committed.

delivery.description: Who may merge a pull request into the default branch (decision 38).

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

mergePolicy.description: manual: the architect asks the owner before every merge. low-risk: the architect may merge, without asking, a pull request that meets every condition of ticket-flow rule 4.

backend.description: The backend the project runs, and how its database tests run.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

kind.description: supabase: packages/supabase, the harness's own. own: a backend of the project's, which the harness does not manage. none: no backend.

databaseTests.description: linked: the pgTAP tests run against the linked Supabase project. local: against a local Supabase stack. off: no database tests run.

then.description: a supabase backend names how its database tests run

else.description: the database-test mode is the supabase backend's only; the harness does not manage the tests of an own backend

vocabulary.description: Terms of the product, beyond its identity, that a portable part of the harness never names.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

forbiddenInCore.description: Proper nouns and unique identifiers only: a generic word that doubles as a domain term would fire on ordinary prose.

stack.description: The stack the project shares with its sibling projects, which a portable part of the harness may name. Each fact is free text, and nothing reads them.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

monorepo.description: The workspace manager and the task runner.

backend.description: The backend, as prose; the backend the harness manages is backend.kind.

core.description: The portable part of the harness, which names no product: the folder a product-name gate walks.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

directory.description: Its path, relative to the repository root.

skills.description: Where the skills live, which of them are vendored, and the design values a first-party skill never copies.

$comment.description: A note for the reader of the section.

trees.description: The folders that hold one skill per folder, relative to the repository root.

lock.description: The lock file whose entries name the vendored skills; a skill with no entry is first-party.

valueSources.description: The files whose hex colours a first-party skill never copies.

valueTerms.description: Design values, such as font families, that a first-party skill never copies.
